why: I64-R1 said that I64 registers no contract on M0-M3, and its test asserted that no committed contract names M0-M3 at all, which holds of I64's own tree but forbids the first real contract any later key registers. I65 (= I33b; tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O8, at the I65 prereg) registers C_o12 on M2 by design. The amended test lets a contract name a real milestone exactly when the I65 key's thresholds.registered_contracts gives its id that milestone ({"C_o12": "M2"}), so any other contract on M0-M3 still fails it. Its record check (no record at the top of results/M0-M3 marked intended_bounded or carrying intended) is unchanged, so it does not see I65's one mark, which is on results/M2/extracted_m1/L_undo_cancel.json and is checked by tests_m3/test_o12.py (I65-P2). I64-R1's own words, 'no M0-M3 record is marked', therefore no longer describe HEAD: an M2 view record carries I65's mark by design. Amended in the I65 prereg commit itself, so the I65 build edits no I64 test for it.

I33 (tests_m3/test_o12_m3.py rules B8 and B12, at the I33 prereg) registers C_o12_m3 on M3, and its proved L_weak marks I71's results/M3 record L_undo_cancel_Rollup_challengeState_setPause intended_bounded (K5). I64-R1's test, as I65 amended it, admits only I65's registered contracts and no marked top-level M3 record, so it would fail on I33's planned outcome. Narrowed to I33's outcome: the I33 key's thresholds.registered_contracts ({C_o12_m3: M3}) join I65's, and a results/M3 record may carry the mark exactly when tests_m3/_i33.expected_marks says C_o12_m3 must mark it. Every other contract and record check is unchanged, so a contract on M0-M3 that no key registers, or a mark no proved contract licenses, still fails.
